newsitem.title: USA: NY precious metals end lower on good volume.
newsitem.headline: NY precious metals end lower on good volume.

text.p: New York precious metals futures ended lower Wednesday, on good volumes, and have now given back about half of the sharp bounce seen last week.

"The good news from a traders point of view is that intraday volatility has risen back up to around $2.00-$3.00 a day and that brings in more liquidity," said Scott Meyers, an analyst with Pioneer Futures in New York.
"We're back in the middle of the road though, after last week's gains, and psychology and the fundamentals are still bearish," he said.
COMEX April gold, now the active contract, ended down $2.50 an ounce at $353.20, but off the session lows at $352.70. Estimated total volume was 68,000 contracts.

Spot gold ended quoted $351,00/50 an ounce, compared to the London Wednesday afternoon fix at $351.10 and the New York close Tuesday at $352.90/40. Spot gold saw a three year low around $347.00 in mid-January.

US durable goods orders data reported early Wednesday, suggested US economic growth remained subdued and inflation no threat, providing little incentive for investors in precious metals, analysts said.
